subject: Science

source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 23 (Skeleton labelling sheet (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 23: The skeleton: support, protection and movement. To understand the functions of the skeleton and how joints allow movement

picture.alt: A labelled diagram of the human skeleton
picture.draw: Draw and label: Skeleton labelling sheet

questions.q: Which bones protect the brain, and what is the joint between them?
questions.model: Name the organ: brain. Which bone surrounds it? The skull. Do skull bones move? No. So they are joined by fixed joints.

questions.a: Cushions the ends of bones and reduces friction.

questions.q: Name one job of bone marrow.
Core: Label a skeleton diagram with 8 bones (skull, ribs, spine, pelvis, femur, humerus, radius, tibia) and three joints.
questions.a: Accept correctly labelled bones and joints.
questions.model: Teacher labels the femur first: thigh bone, the longest bone in the body.

questions.q: Extend: Explain how the skeleton protects three organs.
questions.a: Skull protects brain; ribs protect heart and lungs; spine protects spinal cord.

questions.q: Stretch: Why is it painful if cartilage wears away in a knee?
questions.a: Bone rubs on bone, causing friction, swelling and pain.

questions.q: Big question: why does your body need 206 bones instead of one?
questions.a: Joints between many bones allow movement in different directions.
